description: Change of use from Class C3 (dwellinghouse) to Class C2 (children's home for up to three children).
decision_conditions: The proposed change of use from a C3 dwellinghouse to a C2 children's home would result in the loss of an existing self-contained family dwelling. Whilst the proposed use would provide a form of specialist accommodation and the submitted Written Statement of Local Need is noted, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the loss of the existing family dwelling would be justified in the wider public interest or that this particular property would be suitable for the proposed use. The proposal would therefore conflict with the objective of safeguarding existing housing stock and would fail to demonstrate compliance with the policy requirements for residential care accommodation, contrary to Policies DMH 1 and DMH 8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies H8, H9 and H12 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of the constrained internal layout, limited internal communal living space, and lack of meaningful usable private outdoor amenity space, would fail to provide a satisfactory standard of accommodation for the intended occupiers of the proposed children's home, contrary to Policies DMH 8, DMHB 11 and DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies D3, D6 and H12 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of the siting of two off-street car parking spaces within the rear garden, in close association with the proposed outdoor amenity areas for children aged 7 to 18, would fail to provide a safe, usable and satisfactory external amenity environment for the intended occupiers. In the absence of details demonstrating appropriate separation or management of the parking area from the children's outdoor amenity space, the proposal would create an unacceptable conflict between vehicular activity and private amenity/play space. The development would therefore be contrary to Policies DMH 8, DMHB 11, DMHB 15 and DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies D3, D6 and D11 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed 24-hour staffed C2 children's home, involving up to three children, daytime and overnight staff, staff handovers, manager attendance and associated professional and visitor movements, would operate without causing undue noise, disturbance and general activity harmful to neighbouring occupiers. In the absence of a sufficiently detailed, site-specific and enforceable management framework, and in the absence of any noise assessment, acoustic report, sound insulation details or other mitigation measures, the proposal would fail to safeguard neighbouring residential amenity, contrary to Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies D3, D13 and D14 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed 24-hour staffed C2 use could operate without causing overspill parking, additional parking stress or adverse highway impacts, having regard to staff handovers, manager attendance, professional visits, family/friend visits and other operational movements. In the absence of accurate transport information, enforceable travel arrangements, the proposal has not demonstrated that staff, visitor and operational parking demand would be appropriately accommodated or managed, contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2, DMT 5 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), and Policies T4, T5 and T6 of the London Plan (2021).

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.

In order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably. In addition further guidance was offered to the applicant by the case officer during the processing of the application to identify the amendments to address those elements of the scheme considered unacceptable which the applicant chose not to implement.
